title: ProcDump command targets LSASS by name
description: Detects ProcDump or a renamed ProcDump executable referencing LSASS as a command-line process-name token, including the default mini dump without a size switch. PID-only targeting requires separate process correlation.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use Sysinternals ProcDump to capture LSASS memory and recover credentials.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents that ProcDump writes a mini dump by default without -ma/-mm. LSASS is the process-name signal; KeyIso and SamSs are service labels and do not establish a process target. PID-only requests require a correlated process inventory.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify ProcDump commands naming LSASS with or without dump-size switches. Do not infer LSASS access from PID-only commands, output-file substrings or KeyIso and SamSs service names.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the binary identity, target process and dump destination, then determine whether an authorized diagnostic or response workflow explains the activity.
steps: Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete command, file path, original filename metadata, account, parent process and target endpoint role.
Locate the resulting dump, inspect its destination and access history, and correlate subsequent archive, transfer or credential-use activity.
Confirm an approved diagnostic or incident-response case; contain the endpoint and protect potentially exposed credentials when unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved crash diagnostics, forensic acquisition or incident response involving LSASS

validation.expected_outcome: Match LSASS process-name arguments with optional dump-size switches; reject service labels, PID-only commands, LSASS output-path text, unrelated targets and missing commands.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
